quiz.q: How many bits does ASCII use for each character?
quiz.why: ASCII uses 7 bits per character, which gives 2 to the power of 7 = 128 codes.

quiz.q: What ASCII code is used to store the character '7'?
quiz.why: The digit 0 is 48, so the character 7 is 48 + 7 = 55, not the number 7.

quiz.q: Given that upper-case A is 65, what is the ASCII code for upper-case G?
quiz.why: G is six letters after A, so its code is 65 + 6 = 71.

quiz.q: Why does a sort by character code put a capital Z before a lower-case a?
options: Capital letters are stored in Unicode only
Lower-case letters use more bits each
Z is 90, which is smaller than a at 97
The computer sorts words by their length
quiz.why: Upper-case codes (65 to 90) are all lower numbers than lower-case codes (97 to 122).

quiz.q: Why could old ASCII files still be read after Unicode arrived?
options: Unicode converts every file when opened
Unicode only uses 128 codes in total
ASCII files were stored as pictures
Unicode kept the same codes for 0 to 127
quiz.why: Unicode copied the first 128 ASCII codes, so A is still 65 in both.
